subject: Civil Engineering
title: Speed Design and the Design Vehicle
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Speed Design and the Design Vehicle.

hook.text: A road designed for sports cars fails when an 18-wheeler tries to make the turn.

buildup.text: The design vehicle is the largest vehicle the road must safely accommodate.

discovery.text: Turn radii, lane widths, and clearances are all sized to the design vehicle.

twist.text: Design speed is the maximum safe speed — it governs curve radii and sight distance.

climax.text: Interstate highways design for semi-trucks at 70 mph — every dimension follows from that.

punchline.text: Design for the biggest vehicle at the target speed. Everything else follows.

quiz.question: Why do engineers use a 'design vehicle' in road design?
options: To determine how many vehicles the road can handle daily
To ensure the road safely accommodates the largest expected vehicle
To set the speed limit for the entire road segment
